active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.signal.medfilt for median-based filtering to preserve edges and reduce false reversals
active_paradigms.description: Replace the weighted moving average with scipy.signal.medfilt, which uses median filtering instead of mean. Median filtering is robust to outliers and preserves signal edges better than mean-based smoothing. This directly addresses the false reversal penalty (R) and slope change penalty (S) because median filters don't create spurious directional changes from noise spikes. Apply with an odd kernel size (e.g., window_size if even, add 1). The median naturally rejects noise-induced reversals while maintaining trend direction. This is fundamentally different from the failed Kalman/wavelet approaches as it's a non-parametric, order-statistics based filter.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) and slope changes (S) - the 0.3+0.3=0.6 weight components. Median filtering excels at preserving trend direction while rejecting noise.
active_paradigms.cautions: Kernel size must be odd. May introduce slight lag but less than weighted moving average for edge preservation. Test kernel sizes 5, 7, 9, 11 to find optimal balance.

active_paradigms.idea: Implement adaptive hysteresis-based trend tracking with threshold-based updates
active_paradigms.description: Create a custom trend-tracking algorithm that only updates the filtered output when the input signal crosses a dynamically computed threshold. This prevents noise-induced trend changes. Maintain a running trend estimate and only update it when |current_input - trend_estimate| exceeds a threshold (e.g., 2*std of recent residuals). This directly reduces false reversals (R) and slope changes (S) by ignoring small fluctuations. The threshold can be adaptive based on recent signal variance. This is fundamentally different from smoothing approaches - it's a decision-based filter that preserves genuine trends while rejecting noise.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) and slope changes (S) - hysteresis prevents noise from triggering trend changes. Also improves lag by not smoothing genuine changes.
active_paradigms.cautions: Need to tune threshold parameter carefully - too high causes lag, too low allows false reversals. Use adaptive threshold based on running variance. Handle edge cases when signal is flat.

active_paradigms.idea: Use scipy.stats.mstats.mad with Hampel filter for outlier detection and replacement
active_paradigms.description: Implement Hampel filter using scipy.stats.mstats.mad (median absolute deviation) to detect and replace outliers before any smoothing. The Hampel filter identifies points that deviate more than k*MAD from the local median and replaces them with the median. This preserves the signal structure while removing noise spikes that cause false reversals. After outlier removal, apply minimal smoothing. This approach is fundamentally different - it's outlier-based rather than smoothing-based, and uses robust statistics (median/MAD) instead of mean-based methods.
active_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) and slope changes (S) - removing outliers prevents noise spikes from creating spurious trend changes. Preserves genuine signal dynamics better than aggressive smoothing.
active_paradigms.cautions: Hampel filter needs window size and k parameter (typically k=3 for 99% coverage). Apply before any smoothing. Handle boundary effects carefully.

tried_paradigms.idea: Implement adaptive Kalman filter with constant velocity model
tried_paradigms.description: Replace the weighted moving average with a Kalman filter that maintains state (position and velocity) to predict signal dynamics. The Kalman filter naturally balances tracking the noisy signal (minimizing L_recent/L_avg) with smoothness (minimizing S and R) through its prediction-update cycle. Use a constant velocity state-space model where the state vector contains [position, velocity]. Set process noise Q to handle non-stationarity and measurement noise R based on observed signal variance. The filter will adaptively smooth while tracking genuine trend changes. Implement as a single function using numpy matrix operations without scipy.optimize.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Balance between slope changes (S), lag error (L_recent/L_avg), and false reversals (R) through Kalman gain adaptation
tried_paradigms.cautions: Initialize state covariance properly to avoid filter divergence. Tune Q and R parameters - too high Q causes jitter, too low Q causes lag. Handle edge cases for short signals.

tried_paradigms.idea: Apply Savitzky-Golay filter for polynomial-based smoothing
tried_paradigms.description: Use scipy.signal.savgol_filter to smooth the signal while preserving higher-order polynomial characteristics. The Savitzky-Golay filter fits a polynomial locally to each window and evaluates it at the center point, which preserves signal features like peaks and inflection points better than simple moving averages. Set polynomial order to 2 or 3 for good balance between smoothness and tracking. The window length should match the given window_size parameter (must be odd). This single function call provides smooth output with minimal phase delay and reduced slope changes compared to the current weighted average approach.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) while maintaining tracking accuracy through polynomial feature preservation
tried_paradigms.cautions: Window length must be odd and greater than polynomial order. Use padtype='reflect' or 'nearest' for edge handling. Choose polynomial order 2-3 for non-stationary signals.

tried_paradigms.idea: Use wavelet denoising with soft thresholding
tried_paradigms.description: Apply PyWavelets (pywt) for multi-scale wavelet decomposition and denoising. Decompose the signal using a wavelet family like 'db4' or 'sym4' to separate noise (high-frequency coefficients) from signal components. Apply soft thresholding to wavelet coefficients at each decomposition level using a universal threshold (sigma * sqrt(2*log(N))). Reconstruct the signal from thresholded coefficients. This approach handles multi-frequency signals well (test signal 1-2) and preserves step changes (test signal 3) better than sliding window methods. It's a single function call through pywt.denoise that processes the entire signal at once.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) for multi-frequency signals and step changes, while reducing slope changes through frequency-selective smoothing
tried_paradigms.cautions: Choose appropriate wavelet family (db4, sym4, or coif2). Use 'soft' thresholding for smoother results. Set wavelet decomposition level appropriately (typically 2-4 for these signal lengths).

tried_paradigms.description: Implement Savitzky-Golay filter using scipy.signal.savgol_filter which fits a polynomial to each sliding window and returns the polynomial value at the center. This preserves signal trends and reduces slope changes better than simple moving average. The polynomial order (typically 2-3) and window length (must be odd, slightly less than input window_size) control the trade-off between smoothness and responsiveness. This directly addresses the slope change penalty (S) and false reversal penalty (R) while maintaining reasonable lag error.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: Slope changes (S) and false reversals (R) by preserving trend structure; maintain tracking accuracy through polynomial fitting rather than averaging
tried_paradigms.cautions: Window length must be odd and less than input length; polynomial order should be 2-3 for trend preservation; handle edge cases where signal length < window_size

tried_paradigms.idea: Implement adaptive Kalman filter with state-space modeling
tried_paradigms.description: Build a custom Kalman filter using numpy that models the signal as a state-space system with position and velocity states. The filter adaptively estimates the underlying signal and its slope, with process noise covariance that can be tuned based on observed residuals. This handles non-stationary signals by naturally adapting to changes while filtering noise. The Kalman gain automatically balances between tracking the noisy input (for lag error) and maintaining smooth trends (for slope changes).
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: All four metrics simultaneously by adaptively balancing noise reduction and trend preservation; especially good for non-stationary signals with changing frequency or step changes
tried_paradigms.cautions: Must initialize state covariance properly; tune process noise (Q) and measurement noise (R) parameters; handle edge cases at signal boundaries; ensure numerical stability

tried_paradigms.description: Apply a two-stage filtering approach: first use scipy.ndimage.median_filter to remove outliers and reduce noise-induced slope changes, then apply scipy.signal.savgol_filter to smooth while preserving trends. Median filtering is robust to outliers and reduces spurious reversals, while Savitzky-Golay preserves the underlying signal dynamics. This cascade approach addresses both noise reduction and trend preservation more effectively than either method alone.
tried_paradigms.what_to_optimize: False reversals (R) and slope changes (S) through median filtering, then maintain tracking accuracy (L_avg, L_recent) through Savitzky-Golay smoothing
tried_paradigms.cautions: Median filter size must be odd; ensure cascaded windows don't create excessive lag; handle edge effects from both filters; total processing delay increases with cascade
